note: This is an ADDENDUM to research/audits/loss_inventory.json (v1, untouched, still authoritative for the base facts: free_index=17, ignore_index=255, per-loss numerator/denominator, camera_mask semantics, applied_heads/scales). This file records ONLY what is NEW in the v2 spec pass: per-group gradient NORMS, the allterm_harddrop cross-check, and the RayIoU origin-builder audit.

gradient_norms_at_lambda_0_25.purpose: spec v2 3.1 requires free_logit_gradient_norm / occupied_logit_gradient_norm / inv_free_logit_gradient_norm per loss, not just PASS/FAIL zero-checks.
gradient_norms_at_lambda_0_25.method: same CPU synthetic batch as v1 (seed=4), per-voxel L2 grad norm over the class axis, averaged within each of 4 groups: free_visible, occupied_visible, inv_occupied, inv_free.
gradient_norms_at_lambda_0_25.reading: at lambda=0.25, inv_free's gradient norm is roughly 1/4 of the corresponding visible/inv_occupied groups for CE_focal and sem_scal (consistent with the weight literally being 0.25x), confirming the weighting acts as a real, proportional dampening of gradient magnitude, not merely a bookkeeping artifact that leaves gradients unchanged. geo_scal's inv_free/occupied_visible ratio looks larger because geo_scal's occupied_visible group itself has a tiny norm in this particular synthetic batch (not a general property).

allterm_harddrop.purpose: spec v2 3.1 item 3: a SEPARATE diagnostic mode -- exclude the voxel from every loss's input population entirely (not just weight=0) and confirm direct gradient=0.
allterm_harddrop.method: relabel invisible-free voxels' target to ignore_index=255 (a DIFFERENT code path than voxel_weight=0 -- this is literally what STCOccLoadOccGTFromFileCVPR2023's baseline_with_mask dataset-level policy does), and re-check gradient at those voxels.
allterm_harddrop.result: CE_focal_primitive, sem_scal, geo_scal: all PASS, exact zero gradient, via this independent mechanism -- corroborates the weight=0 result was not an artifact of how voxel_weight=0 happens to interact with these specific formulas.
allterm_harddrop.lovasz: NOT_TESTED via this synthetic harness in the 'weight=0' sense (never applicable, lovasz has no weight param at the call site) -- BUT ignore_index=255 relabeling DOES work on lovasz_softmax when exercised directly (see lovasz_relative_share test, which calls lovasz_softmax with the SAME ignore_index mechanism successfully). The finding is therefore precise: lovasz_softmax's OWN ignore_index support is fine; the issue is only that get_voxel_loss's lambda_inv_free mechanism never routes through it -- lambda never touches lovasz's target at all, at any lambda value.

lovasz_relative_share_vs_lambda.purpose: template explicitly sets `assume_lower_lambda_increases_lovasz_relative_effect: false` -- i.e. check, do not assume.
lovasz_relative_share_vs_lambda.method: on the same synthetic batch, computed lovasz_softmax's own (unweighted, exactly as it runs in real training) gradient norm at the inv_free voxels, and the COMBINED (sum-of-squares) norm of the other 3 losses at the same voxels under lambda in {1.0, 0.25, 0.0}, then lovasz_share = lovasz_norm / (lovasz_norm + other3_norm).
lovasz_relative_share_vs_lambda.reading: CONFIRMED (not merely assumed) directionally: lovasz's share of total inv_free gradient magnitude does increase monotonically as lambda decreases, trivially reaching 100% at lambda=0 (since the other 3 are then exactly zero there). More importantly: at lambda=1.0 (the historical w/o-mask baseline, i.e. what ALL 6 legacy runs before lambda=0 experienced at these voxels) lovasz's share is only ~0.4% -- i.e. on this synthetic batch, lovasz's ABSOLUTE contribution at invisible-free voxels is small compared to what the other 3 losses contribute when lambda=1. This is evidence (not proof) that the 'lambda=0 is not a true hard-drop' caveat, while categorically correct, may correspond to a SMALL residual magnitude rather than a large one -- but this was measured on random synthetic logits, not on a converged real checkpoint's actual logit distribution, so the magnitude comparison should NOT be extrapolated to the real training runs without re-measuring on real batches (flagged explicitly, per the template's own caution against assuming).

new_bug_found.description: `import numpy as np` appears inside BOTH the `if isinstance(labels, list):` branch AND the `elif isinstance(labels, np.ndarray):` branch. Because the import statement's mere textual presence anywhere in the function body makes Python treat `np` as function-local for the WHOLE function, evaluating the `elif isinstance(labels, np.ndarray)` condition itself raises `UnboundLocalError: local variable 'np' referenced before assignment` whenever the `if isinstance(labels, list)` branch was NOT taken (e.g. labels is a bare torch.Tensor).
new_bug_found.reproduced: yes, directly, in this audit's test script, by calling lovasz_softmax(probas, target_as_bare_tensor, ignore=255) -- confirmed crash, then confirmed the fix (wrapping target in list(...) before the call) avoids it because that forces the `if isinstance(labels, list)` branch, which imports numpy first.
new_bug_found.real_training_impact: NONE OBSERVED in the 6 completed legacy runs -- `target_voxel_semantic` (and its multi-scale siblings) arrive at this call site as a python list in every real training/eval invocation in this repo (confirmed in the v1 audit: mmengine's collate does not stack these particular Collect3D keys), so the `list` branch is always taken and the bug never fires. This is a LATENT bug (real, reproducible, pre-existing, not introduced by any lambda-weighting change) that would only manifest if some future code path ever passed a bare tensor/ndarray to lovasz_softmax's `labels` argument.
new_bug_found.recommended_fix: move `import numpy as np` to the top of lovasz_softmax.py (module level) instead of inside either branch. Trivial, zero behavior change for any currently-working call site. NOT applied in this audit pass (audit-only, no code changes).

new_bug_found_e1_export_sampler_duplicat.discovered_during: E1 logit export (research_v2/tools -- export_occ_logits.py run on the 1202-sample calibration split)
new_bug_found_e1_export_sampler_duplicat.description: __len__ reports len(dataset) (e.g. 1202), but __iter__'s actual eval-time bound is `t = (len(flag) + world_size*16 + 1) // world_size`, then `range(t // batch_size)` -- NOT range(len(dataset)). With world_size=1, batch_size=1, this yields exactly len(dataset)+17 iterations (verified: 1202 -> 1219 observed in 3 separate export runs, all reproducing the same +17). The extra iterations are a deterministic wraparound: after the single `torch.randperm` cycle over all scene-groups exhausts (draining every group's samples exactly once, since sum(group_sizes)==len(dataset)), the generator immediately starts a second reshuffled cycle over the SAME static group->sample-index lists, so the +17 'extra' exports are exact re-reads of already-exported dataset rows -- confirmed by tracing group_idx_to_sample_idxs (built once, deterministic) and the _infinite_group_indices generator, NOT random/misaligned data.
new_bug_found_e1_export_sampler_duplicat.scope_of_impact: Any code that manually iterates this dataloader without its own index-based dedup (as tools/export_occ_logits.py originally did) will silently double-export ~17 samples per ~1200-sample subset (scaling roughly with world_size*16/N). mmengine's own TestLoop.run() has the identical unbounded-iteration behavior (grep-confirmed, no max_iters passed), so this is a property of the sampler class itself, not specific to our new script.
new_bug_found_e1_export_sampler_duplicat.why_legacy_mIoU_and_RayIoU_numbers_are_N: occupancy_metric.py already guards against exactly this with index-based `processed_set`/`_f_processed_set` dedup at multiple call sites (compute_metrics_from_file, _compute_rayiou, uncertainty extraction -- lines ~525,620,995-1076,1455-1472), each with a 'CRITICAL: Skip duplicates' comment. This means someone already discovered and defended against this exact sampler behavior for the metrics that matter; the 6 legacy runs' reported mIoU/RayIoU numbers are not believed to be corrupted by it.
new_bug_found_e1_export_sampler_duplicat.fix_applied: tools/export_occ_logits.py now dedups by each sample's `index` field (the same field OccupancyMetric already keys its processed_set on), matching the codebase's established defensive pattern. This IS a real code change (not audit-only, unlike the Lovasz bug above), since it directly affects E1's own output correctness. The sampler's own off-by-N length formula was NOT touched (out of scope, would affect other consumers unpredictably; the dedup-at-the-consumer pattern is what the rest of the codebase already relies on).
new_bug_found_e1_export_sampler_duplicat.not_touched: infinite_group_each_sample_in_batch_sampler.py itself -- the len(flag)+world_size*16+1 formula looks like an intentional multi-GPU-safety over-provision (so no rank starves early) rather than a bug to 'fix' at the source; changing it risks the opposite failure mode (a rank stopping early) for actual distributed training/eval, which is out of scope for this diagnostic pass.

rayiou_origin_builder_audit.purpose: spec v2 3.2 + E2 prerequisite: read the ACTUAL local RayIoU origin builder, do not assume it matches the SparseOcc paper description or the model's actual input window.
rayiou_origin_builder_audit.finding_1_origins_span_the_whole_scene_n: nuScenesDataset.__getitem__ iterates `curr_index in range(len(self.valid_index))` -- i.e. EVERY sample in the ENTIRE val split -- and keeps any `curr_index` whose `scene_tokens[curr_index] == ref_scene_token`, WITH NO RESTRICTION on curr_index being before or after ref_index. This means candidate lidar origins include BOTH past AND future samples from anywhere in the same scene, entirely independent of the model's actual 16-frame input history window (which is a separate, single-step-relative `curr_to_prev_ego_rt` recurrence tracked in nuscenes_dataset_occ.py, confirmed unrelated code path).
rayiou_origin_builder_audit.finding_2_spatial_filter_and_subsample: candidate origins are filtered to `abs(x)<39 and abs(y)<39` (inside the occupancy volume), then if more than 8 remain, uniformly subsampled BY INDEX POSITION (np.linspace over the ordered list, not by time) down to exactly 8. The final origin set for a given sample is therefore some mix of past+future poses actually used for RayIoU scoring, with NO metadata retained about which of the (up to) 8 origins is 'current' vs 'past' vs 'future' relative to the reference frame.
rayiou_origin_builder_audit.finding_3_renderer_is_cuda_only: process_one_sample calls `dvr.render_forward(occ_pred.cuda(), ...)` unconditionally -- this ray-casting/depth-rendering step is GPU-only, cannot be exercised in a CPU-only P0 pass. Confirmed via code reading only, not executed in this audit.
rayiou_origin_builder_audit.finding_4_tp_fp_fn_rule: calc_metrics computes, per class per threshold in {1,2,4} meters: TP = same predicted&GT class at a ray point AND |pred_depth - gt_depth| < threshold; IoU_class = TP/(GT_count+Pred_count-TP). This matches the standard RayIoU definition. The exact 'GT no-hit ray exclusion' behavior lives inside the `dvr.render_forward` CUDA extension itself (not Python-traceable in this pass) -- NOT independently re-derived in this audit; no evidence found of local deviation from upstream SparseOcc behavior, but this specific sub-claim is UNVERIFIED, not confirmed.
rayiou_origin_builder_audit.consequence_for_this_research: This is the single most important NEW factual finding of the v2 P0 pass: RayIoU as currently computed in this repo is NOT restricted to origins the model could actually have observed from its real 16-frame input history -- it can and does draw ego-lidar origins from later (future, relative to the reference frame) points in the same driving scene. This directly matters for interpreting any RayIoU gain: part of a model's RayIoU credit for correctly predicting 'hidden free' space could be confirmed via an origin that was never available as model input, which is exactly the kind of origin-provenance question spec v2 E2 is designed to decompose (origin_time_group, origin_in_actual_input_window). No conclusion is drawn here about how MUCH of the lambda-sweep's RayIoU gain this affects -- that is E2's job, not P0's.
rayiou_origin_builder_audit.not_yet_done: Cross-referencing actual per-sample origin timestamps against the model's actual input-window timestamps (to compute origin_time_group and origin_in_actual_input_window per spec 5.2) has NOT been done in this P0 pass -- it requires instrumenting nuScenesDataset.__getitem__ to also emit per-origin timestamps/sample_tokens (currently only the final 3D offset vector is returned, not which sample/timestamp it came from), which is exactly what E2's planned evaluator change targets (see research_v2/reports/E2_execution_plan.md).
